title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
modernization_rationale: 1925 American prose is largely accessible to modern readers; only occasional period idioms (bond business, rotogravure, Teutonic migration) and 1920s slang need light touch. Fitzgerald's cadence must be preserved; don't modernize the sentences themselves.

segments.title: I

signatures.passage_hint: In my younger and more vulnerable years my father gave me some advice that I've been turning over in my mind ever since.
signatures.why: The novel's iconic opening sentence.

signatures.passage_hint: Whenever you feel like criticizing anyone, he told me, just remember that all the people in this world haven't had the advantages that you've had.
signatures.why: Among the most quoted lines in American fiction; the ethical frame Nick will betray.

signatures.passage_hint: Reserving judgements is a matter of infinite hope. I am still a little afraid of missing something if I forget that, as my father snobbishly suggested, and I snobbishly repeat, a sense of the fundamental decencies is parcelled out unequally at birth.
signatures.why: Voice-establishing: Nick's self-aware snobbery, the cadence on which the unreliable-narrator reading turns.

signatures.passage_hint: If personality is an unbroken series of successful gestures, then there was something gorgeous about him, some heightened sensitivity to the promises of life
signatures.why: The novel's thesis statement about Gatsby.

signatures.passage_hint: it was an extraordinary gift for hope, a romantic readiness such as I have never found in any other person and which it is not likely I shall ever find again.
signatures.why: 'Romantic readiness' is critically load-bearing.

signatures.passage_hint: it is what preyed on Gatsby, what foul dust floated in the wake of his dreams that temporarily closed out my interest in the abortive sorrows and short-winded elations of men.
signatures.why: The 'foul dust' framing — closes the preamble's ethical argument.

signatures.passage_hint: The only completely stationary object in the room was an enormous couch on which two young women were buoyed up as though upon an anchored balloon.
signatures.why: Signature set-piece prose establishing Daisy and Jordan as ethereal.

signatures.passage_hint: They were both in white, and their dresses were rippling and fluttering as if they had just been blown back in after a short flight around the house.
signatures.why: The flight imagery — frequently anthologized Fitzgerald style.

signatures.passage_hint: I hope she'll be a fool—that's the best thing a girl can be in this world, a beautiful little fool.
signatures.why: Central to feminist readings of Daisy; one of the novel's most quoted lines.

signatures.passage_hint: he stretched out his arms toward the dark water in a curious way, and, far as I was from him, I could have sworn he was trembling.
signatures.why: The green light's first appearance — the novel's central symbol.

signatures.passage_hint: distinguished nothing except a single green light, minute and far away, that might have been the end of a dock.
signatures.why: The green light — universally recognized signature image.

signatures.passage_hint: Her face was sad and lovely with bright things in it, bright eyes and a bright passionate mouth, but there was an excitement in her voice that men who had cared for her found difficult to forget
signatures.why: Voice-establishing rendering of Daisy's charm — seeds the later 'voice full of money.'

segments.notes: Longest preamble in the book; do not over-cut the opening ethical frame or the green-light closing. Compress dinner-party small talk (Tom's Goddard rant, the butler-nose anecdote) but keep the 'Nordic' beat and Daisy's 'sophisticated' aria. Preserve the Buchanan-house tableau of the two women on the couch — this is the book's visual signature. End with the green light intact.

segments.title: II

signatures.passage_hint: This is a valley of ashes—a fantastic farm where ashes grow like wheat into ridges and hills and grotesque gardens
signatures.why: Canonical set-piece and major symbol.

signatures.passage_hint: where ashes take the forms of houses and chimneys and rising smoke and, finally, with a transcendent effort, of ash-grey men
signatures.why: The ash-men image — load-bearing for economic readings.

signatures.passage_hint: the eyes of Doctor T. J. Eckleburg. The eyes of Doctor T. J. Eckleburg are blue and gigantic—their retinas are one yard high.
signatures.why: Iconic image, later weaponized as 'God sees everything.'

signatures.passage_hint: They look out of no face, but, instead, from a pair of enormous yellow spectacles which pass over a nonexistent nose.
signatures.why: The spectacles-without-face — completes the Eckleburg icon.

signatures.passage_hint: With the influence of the dress her personality had also undergone a change. The intense vitality that had been so remarkable in the garage was converted into impressive hauteur.
signatures.why: Register-defining satirical mode; Nick's class observation of Myrtle.

signatures.passage_hint: I was within and without, simultaneously enchanted and repelled by the inexhaustible variety of life.
signatures.why: Nick's signature self-definition — the detached observer stance.

signatures.passage_hint: Making a short deft movement, Tom Buchanan broke her nose with his open hand.
signatures.why: Plot hinge rendered in a single prosodically stark sentence.

segments.notes: Compress hard through the apartment party — Catherine, the McKees, and the dog-buying can be trimmed to essentials, but keep Myrtle's social performance (the vitality-to-hauteur transformation) and her list of things to get. Preserve the valley-of-ashes opening in full and the Eckleburg eyes verbatim. The nose-breaking sentence must land unfiltered. Close with the McKee bedroom/Penn Station fragment — the elliptical collage is voice.

segments.title: III

signatures.passage_hint: In his blue gardens men and girls came and went like moths among the whisperings and the champagne and the stars.
signatures.why: Signature Fitzgerald sentence; the moths simile is iconic.

signatures.passage_hint: Every Friday five crates of oranges and lemons arrived from a fruiterer in New York—every Monday these same oranges and lemons left his back door in a pyramid of pulpless halves.
signatures.why: Signature catalogue-of-excess mode.

signatures.passage_hint: By seven o'clock the orchestra has arrived, no thin five-piece affair, but a whole pitful of oboes and trombones and saxophones and viols and cornets and piccolos
signatures.why: The present-tense party set-piece — prosodically unmistakable.

signatures.passage_hint: The lights grow brighter as the earth lurches away from the sun, and now the orchestra is playing yellow cocktail music, and the opera of voices pitches a key higher.
signatures.why: 'Yellow cocktail music' and 'opera of voices' — anthologized lyrical prose.

signatures.passage_hint: He smiled understandingly—much more than understandingly. It was one of those rare smiles with a quality of eternal reassurance in it, that you may come across four or five times in life.
signatures.why: The famous Gatsby's-smile paragraph.

signatures.passage_hint: Precisely at that point it vanished—and I was looking at an elegant young roughneck, a year or two over thirty, whose elaborate formality of speech just missed being absurd.
signatures.why: 'Elegant young roughneck' — the first crack in Gatsby's performance.

signatures.passage_hint: Absolutely real—have pages and everything. I thought they'd be a nice durable cardboard.
signatures.why: Owl Eyes in the library — signature comic-philosophical scene.

signatures.passage_hint: I know nothing whatever about mechanics, he said decisively.
signatures.why: Owl Eyes at the wreck — voice of detached American absurdity.

signatures.passage_hint: You don't understand, explained the criminal. I wasn't driving. There's another man in the car.
signatures.why: The detached-wheel scene — signature comic set-piece.

signatures.passage_hint: At the enchanted metropolitan twilight I felt a haunting loneliness sometimes, and felt it in others—poor young clerks who loitered in front of windows waiting until it was time for a solitary restaurant dinner
signatures.why: Register-defining urban melancholy.

signatures.passage_hint: Everyone suspects himself of at least one of the cardinal virtues, and this is mine: I am one of the few honest people that I have ever known.
signatures.why: The chapter's famous closing line — pivot of unreliable-narrator readings.

segments.notes: The chapter's set-pieces are the preservation priority: blue gardens, oranges-and-lemons, seven-o'clock orchestra, Gatsby's smile, Owl Eyes (library + wreck), and Nick's own New-York-at-twilight digression. Compress the party dialogue (Lucille, the Mumbles, the rumors about Gatsby killing a man — keep one rumor, cut the others to a gesture) and the Jordan-Baker golf-cheating backstory. Close on the 'few honest people' line.

segments.title: IV

signatures.passage_hint: From East Egg, then, came the Chester Beckers and the Leeches, and a man named Bunsen, whom I knew at Yale, and Doctor Webster Civet, who was drowned last summer up in Maine.
signatures.why: The mock-Homeric catalogue — a signature of Nick's ironic voice.

signatures.passage_hint: Snell was there three days before he went to the penitentiary, so drunk out on the gravel drive that Mrs. Ulysses Swett's automobile ran over his right hand.
signatures.why: Catalogue detail that carries the register; delete and the whole list collapses.

signatures.passage_hint: I lived like a young rajah in all the capitals of Europe—Paris, Venice, Rome—collecting jewels, chiefly rubies, hunting big game, painting a little
signatures.why: Gatsby's self-invented biography — the threadbare phrases that make Nick nearly laugh.

signatures.passage_hint: Little Montenegro! He lifted up the words and nodded at them—with his smile.
signatures.why: Voice-establishing middle passage; Nick's irony about Gatsby's performance.

signatures.passage_hint: Over the great bridge, with the sunlight through the girders making a constant flicker upon the moving cars, with the city rising up across the river in white heaps and sugar lumps
signatures.why: Signature lyrical aside; widely quoted.

signatures.passage_hint: The city seen from the Queensboro Bridge is always the city seen for the first time, in its first wild promise of all the mystery and the beauty in the world.
signatures.why: Anthologized New-York-romanticism set-piece.

signatures.passage_hint: Anything can happen now that we've slid over this bridge, I thought; anything at all
signatures.why: Famous coda — 'Even Gatsby could happen.'

signatures.passage_hint: A small, flat-nosed Jew raised his large head and regarded me with two fine growths of hair which luxuriated in either nostril.
signatures.why: Signature grotesque-comic description; critically engaged.

signatures.passage_hint: He's the man who fixed the World's Series back in 1919.
signatures.why: Plot-pivotal revelation rendered with signature Nick flatness.

signatures.passage_hint: Gatsby bought that house so that Daisy would be just across the bay.
signatures.why: Structural pivot of the novel — the revelation that reframes everything.

signatures.passage_hint: He had waited five years and bought a mansion where he dispensed starlight to casual moths—so that he could come over some afternoon to a stranger's garden.
signatures.why: Critically central framing; the 'starlight to casual moths' image recurs in criticism.

signatures.passage_hint: There are only the pursued, the pursuing, the busy, and the tired.
signatures.why: Register-defining aphorism closing the chapter.

segments.notes: Keep a meaningful slice of the Gatsby-guests catalogue — it's the book's satirical core and compression will be tempted to gut it. Preserve Gatsby's tall-tale autobiography (Oxford, Montenegro, San Francisco-as-Middle-West) with Nick's sidelong skepticism. The Queensboro Bridge lyrical passage must survive intact. Wolfshiem's introduction can be compressed but keep the molars, the Oggsford fixation, and the World's Series revelation. Jordan's retrospective of Louisville 1917 is the structural pivot — preserve the 'Gatsby bought that house' line verbatim.

segments.title: V

signatures.passage_hint: Gatsby, pale as death, with his hands plunged like weights in his coat pockets, was standing in a puddle of water glaring tragically into my eyes.
signatures.why: Iconic comic-pathetic image; the puddle is canonical.

signatures.passage_hint: His head leaned back so far that it rested against the face of a defunct mantelpiece clock
signatures.why: The clock scene — signature stagecraft of Gatsby's nerves.

signatures.passage_hint: They're such beautiful shirts, she sobbed, her voice muffled in the thick folds. It makes me sad because I've never seen such—such beautiful shirts before.
signatures.why: Central to readings of Daisy's materialism.

signatures.passage_hint: shirts with stripes and scrolls and plaids in coral and apple-green and lavender and faint orange, with monograms of indian blue
signatures.why: The prosodic run-up that makes the shirts scene land.

signatures.passage_hint: His count of enchanted objects had diminished by one.
signatures.why: The moment the green light loses its symbolic charge.

signatures.passage_hint: Compared to the great distance that had separated him from Daisy it had seemed very near to her, almost touching her. It had seemed as close as a star to the moon.
signatures.why: Load-bearing commentary on dream-object collapse.

signatures.passage_hint: There must have been moments even that afternoon when Daisy tumbled short of his dreams—not through her own fault, but because of the colossal vitality of his illusion.
signatures.why: 'Colossal vitality of his illusion' — canonical critical phrase.

signatures.passage_hint: No amount of fire or freshness can challenge what a man can store up in his ghostly heart.
signatures.why: Closing meditation — signature Fitzgerald aphorism.

signatures.passage_hint: I think that voice held him most, with its fluctuating, feverish warmth, because it couldn't be over-dreamed—that voice was a deathless song.
signatures.why: Seeds the later 'voice full of money.'

segments.notes: This is the reunion scene — preservation priority. Keep the puddle entrance, the clock, the shirts, and the closing meditation intact. Compress Klipspringer/the house tour/the phone interruption but do not cut the green-light diminishment passage. Daisy's 'pink cloud' line is voice-useful and cheap to keep.

segments.title: VI

signatures.passage_hint: The truth was that Jay Gatsby of West Egg, Long Island, sprang from his Platonic conception of himself. He was a son of God
signatures.why: Among the most-cited sentences in American literary criticism.

signatures.passage_hint: he must be about His Father's business, the service of a vast, vulgar, and meretricious beauty.
signatures.why: Load-bearing phrase for every reading of Gatsby's idealism.

signatures.passage_hint: I suppose he'd had the name ready for a long time, even then. His parents were shiftless and unsuccessful farm people—his imagination had never really accepted them as his parents at all.
signatures.why: Critically important for readings of self-invention.

signatures.passage_hint: A universe of ineffable gaudiness spun itself out in his brain while the clock ticked on the washstand and the moon soaked with wet light his tangled clothes upon the floor.
signatures.why: Signature lyrical passage on the young Gatz's imagination.

signatures.passage_hint: a promise that the rock of the world was founded securely on a fairy's wing.
signatures.why: Register-defining metaphysical aside.

signatures.passage_hint: Can't repeat the past? he cried incredulously. Why of course you can!
signatures.why: The novel's most-quoted dialogue exchange — thesis of Gatsby's tragedy.

signatures.passage_hint: So he waited, listening for a moment longer to the tuning-fork that had been struck upon a star. Then he kissed her.
signatures.why: Canonical lyrical set-piece.

signatures.passage_hint: His heart beat faster as Daisy's white face came up to his own. He knew that when he kissed this girl, and forever wed his unutterable visions to her perishable breath, his mind would never romp again like the mind of God.
signatures.why: 'Perishable breath' / 'mind of God' — canonical in Fitzgerald criticism.

signatures.passage_hint: At his lips' touch she blossomed for him like a flower and the incarnation was complete.
signatures.why: Completes the kiss set-piece; load-bearing closing.

segments.notes: Compress the Dan Cody back-story to its essentials (yacht, Ella Kaye, the twenty-five thousand never received) but preserve the 'Platonic conception of himself' paragraph verbatim and the closing flashback (autumn sidewalk, ladder, tuning-fork, kiss). The Tom-on-horseback visit and the Daisy-at-Gatsby's-party passage can be tightened but keep 'she was appalled by West Egg' and 'you can't repeat the past.'

segments.title: VII

signatures.passage_hint: the next day was broiling, almost the last, certainly the warmest, of the summer
signatures.why: The chapter's opening atmospheric — the heat motif that structures the whole.

signatures.passage_hint: Gatsby and I in turn leaned down and took the small reluctant hand. Afterward he kept looking at the child with surprise. I don't think he had ever really believed in its existence before.
signatures.why: Pammy's appearance — load-bearing for every reading of Gatsby's dream.

signatures.passage_hint: Her voice is full of money, he said suddenly.
signatures.why: Among the most-quoted lines in American fiction.

signatures.passage_hint: That was it. I'd never understood before. It was full of money—that was the inexhaustible charm that rose and fell in it, the jingle of it, the cymbals' song of it
signatures.why: Most condensed statement of the novel's economic-romantic theme.

signatures.passage_hint: High in a white palace the king's daughter, the golden girl
signatures.why: 'Golden girl' coda — canonical.

signatures.passage_hint: I suppose the latest thing is to sit back and let Mr. Nobody from Nowhere make love to your wife.
signatures.why: Tom's libertine-to-prig transition — voice-defining for the confrontation.

signatures.passage_hint: Your wife doesn't love you, said Gatsby. She's never loved you. She loves me.
signatures.why: The Plaza confrontation hinge.

signatures.passage_hint: Oh, you want too much! she cried to Gatsby. I love you now—isn't that enough? I can't help what's past.
signatures.why: Daisy's breaking point — load-bearing.

signatures.passage_hint: only the dead dream fought on as the afternoon slipped away, trying to touch what was no longer tangible, struggling unhappily, undespairingly, toward that lost voice across the room.
signatures.why: Critically central — the dream's death at the Plaza.

signatures.passage_hint: Thirty—the promise of a decade of loneliness, a thinning list of single men to know, a thinning briefcase of enthusiasm, thinning hair.
signatures.why: Signature anaphoric melancholy; often anthologized.

signatures.passage_hint: So we drove on toward death through the cooling twilight.
signatures.why: Prosodically unmistakable; widely cited.

signatures.passage_hint: Myrtle Wilson, her life violently extinguished, knelt in the road and mingled her thick dark blood with the dust.
signatures.why: The accident's signature image.

signatures.passage_hint: her left breast was swinging loose like a flap
signatures.why: Shockingly specific detail that the scene turns on; not to be softened.

signatures.passage_hint: So I walked away and left him standing there in the moonlight—watching over nothing.
signatures.why: Chapter's closing image — canonical.

segments.notes: The longest chapter and the plot crux; compression target is aggressive but the signature density is high. Preserve in full: the heat opening, Pammy's appearance, 'Her voice is full of money' + the golden-girl paragraph, the Plaza confrontation (Daisy's 'you want too much' and the 'dead dream fought on' reflection), the drive back with the thirty-years-old passage ending 'toward death through the cooling twilight,' Myrtle's death rendered unsparingly, and the closing 'watching over nothing.' Compress Michaelis-at-the-garage exposition to essentials. The Biloxi digression at the Plaza can be shortened but not cut — it carries the tonal lull before the explosion. Tom's confrontation with Wilson at the gas station should preserve Wilson's sickness and the Eckleburg callback.

segments.title: VIII

signatures.passage_hint: She was the first nice girl he had ever known. In various unrevealed capacities he had come in contact with such people, but always with indiscernible barbed wire between.
signatures.why: Voice-establishing on Gatsby and class — load-bearing for every reading.

signatures.passage_hint: he took Daisy one still October night, took her because he had no real right to touch her hand.
signatures.why: Signature rendering of Gatsby's self-knowledge; prosodically unmistakable.

signatures.passage_hint: But he knew that he was in Daisy's house by a colossal accident.
signatures.why: Critically load-bearing on the social gap.

signatures.passage_hint: gleaming like silver, safe and proud above the hot struggles of the poor.
signatures.why: Daisy-as-silver image — thematic keystone.

signatures.passage_hint: All night the saxophones wailed the hopeless comment of the Beale Street Blues while a hundred pairs of golden and silver slippers shuffled the shining dust.
signatures.why: Register-defining lyrical interlude on Daisy's postwar year.

signatures.passage_hint: He must have felt that he had lost the old warm world, paid a high price for living too long with a single dream.
signatures.why: The 'old warm world' — canonical on Gatsby's death.

signatures.passage_hint: A new world, material without being real, where poor ghosts, breathing dreams like air, drifted fortuitously about
signatures.why: Signature metaphysical set-piece preceding the murder.

signatures.passage_hint: They're a rotten crowd, I shouted across the lawn. You're worth the whole damn bunch put together.
signatures.why: Nick's moral judgment crystallized.

signatures.passage_hint: His gorgeous pink rag of a suit made a bright spot of colour against the white steps
signatures.why: Final visual of Gatsby alive — signature image.

segments.notes: Preserve the Louisville back-story (first 'nice' girl, barbed wire, Daisy-as-silver) — this is where Gatsby's class consciousness is explicit. Compress Wilson/Michaelis vigil to essentials but keep the Eckleburg-as-God moment. Preserve the pool passage in full: 'old warm world,' 'ashen fantastic figure,' and the 'holocaust was complete' close. The 'They're a rotten crowd' shout must land unhedged. Telephone call with Jordan and the Tom-Wilson aftermath in ch9 is referenced here by structure; keep the Klipspringer shoe phone call for ch9, not here.

segments.title: IX

signatures.passage_hint: Let me know about the funeral etc do not know his family at all.
signatures.why: Wolfshiem's letter — signature small-compass character writing.

signatures.passage_hint: He opened it at the back cover and turned it around for me to see. On the last flyleaf was printed the word schedule, and the date September 12, 1906.
signatures.why: The Hopalong Cassidy schedule — iconic biographical artifact.

signatures.passage_hint: The poor son-of-a-bitch, he said.
signatures.why: Owl Eyes at the grave — signature closing note.

signatures.passage_hint: That's my Middle West—not the wheat or the prairies or the lost Swede towns, but the thrilling returning trains of my youth, and the street lamps and sleigh bells in the frosty dark
signatures.why: Load-bearing regionalist passage; voice-establishing.

signatures.passage_hint: I see it as a night scene by El Greco: a hundred houses, at once conventional and grotesque, crouching under a sullen, overhanging sky and a lustreless moon.
signatures.why: The El Greco vision of West Egg — canonical.

signatures.passage_hint: They were careless people, Tom and Daisy—they smashed up things and creatures and then retreated back into their money or their vast carelessness
signatures.why: Among the most-quoted indictments in American literature.

signatures.passage_hint: a fresh, green breast of the new world. Its vanished trees, the trees that had made way for Gatsby's house, had once pandered in whispers to the last and greatest of all human dreams
signatures.why: Canonical American-dream set-piece.

signatures.passage_hint: face to face for the last time in history with something commensurate to his capacity for wonder.
signatures.why: 'Capacity for wonder' — anchors readings of the American-dream thesis.

signatures.passage_hint: Gatsby believed in the green light, the orgiastic future that year by year recedes before us.
signatures.why: Iconic penultimate passage.

signatures.passage_hint: So we beat on, boats against the current, borne back ceaselessly into the past.
signatures.why: The novel's famous closing sentence.

segments.notes: Final chapter — highest compression ratio because the funeral aftermath tolerates summary, but the closing four paragraphs (El Greco vision, careless people, fresh green breast, boats against the current) must be preserved essentially intact. Compress the Slagle phone call, the Wolfshiem office visit (keep Wolfshiem's letter verbatim — it's signature), and Tom Buchanan encounter on Fifth Avenue. The Hopalong Cassidy schedule is iconic — keep the list and the 'General Resolves' structure; Mr. Gatz's pride and the photograph detail frame it. The Jordan farewell scene can be tightened but keep 'You said a bad driver was only safe until she met another bad driver.'

motifs.name: The green light
motifs.description: The single green light at the end of Daisy's dock across the bay — first symbol of Gatsby's unreachable dream, diminished in ch5 when Daisy is actually present, resurrected as 'orgiastic future' in the closing.
indicative_phrases: a single green light, minute and far away
count of enchanted objects had diminished by one

motifs.name: Eckleburg's eyes / valley of ashes
motifs.description: The billboard oculist's gigantic blue eyes looking over the ash-pits — later read by Wilson as God. The ash-grey men and the Eckleburg billboard together form the novel's moral-industrial landscape.
indicative_phrases: eyes of Doctor T. J. Eckleburg

motifs.name: Voice, gold, and money
motifs.description: Daisy's voice and her association with whiteness, silver, and gold — culminating in 'her voice is full of money' and the 'golden girl.'
indicative_phrases: the king's daughter, the golden girl

motifs.name: White / careless aristocracy
motifs.description: Daisy and Jordan's whiteness; the Buchanans' wealth as a kind of destructive weightlessness that retreats into itself.

motifs.name: The dream, the past, the capacity for wonder
motifs.description: Gatsby's Platonic self-invention, the insistence that the past can be repeated, and Nick's closing historical frame.

motifs.name: Moths, parties, and the catalogue
motifs.description: The party guests as moths, the catalogue-of-names, the mock-epic enumeration — Nick's satirical register on the Jazz Age.
indicative_phrases: five crates of oranges and lemons

plan_notes:
Voice is everything here; paraphrase is the real danger. Nick's sentences move in long balanced cadences with embedded irony — do not chop them into modern declaratives. Preserve sentence-level rhythm especially in the famous passages (opening, green light, Gatsby's smile, 'Platonic conception,' 'voice full of money,' Plaza confrontation, 'watching over nothing,' closing pages). 

Period register: keep 'bond business,' 'rotogravure,' 'bootlegger,' 'the Great War,' 'coupé,' 'hydroplane,' 'Oxford man,' 'Montenegro' — modernization would flatten the world. Fitzgerald's 'negro' and Wolfshiem's antisemitic caricature are period markers that scholarship engages directly; preserve the Wolfshiem description as written (it is textually signature and critically discussed). Do not sanitize Tom's 'Rise of the Coloured Empires' rant — it is character evidence.

Indirection: Nick is an unreliable narrator and the book trades on what he chooses not to say (his own engagement back home, his feelings for Jordan, the 'second sight' he gives Tom). Preserve the hedges — 'I suppose,' 'I think,' 'I have an idea' — rather than resolving them into fact.

Difficult passages: the Dan Cody back-story (ch6) compresses cleanly but the 'Platonic conception of himself' paragraph must remain word-for-word. The Plaza confrontation (ch7) is long but the dialogue is structurally load-bearing — cut narration around it, not the lines. The closing pages (ch9) are the book's most-quoted material and should be preserved at something close to full length; take compression from the Wolfshiem office visit, Slagle call, and Jordan farewell instead.

Chapter budgets sum to ~21,317 which leaves ~2000 words of headroom against the 23,317 target — allocated to the three signature-heaviest chapters (I, III, VII) if needed.
